independence_note: New evaluation questions authored separately from the development dataset. Do not use this set for prompt or repair tuning.

tests.question: Which suppliers have products with an average rating above 4.5? Show supplier names and average ratings.
tests.reference_sql: SELECT s.name AS supplier_name, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS average_rating FROM suppliers s JOIN products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.name HAVING AVG(r.rating) > 4.5 ORDER BY average_rating DESC, s.supplier_id

tests.question: Which customers have placed orders in at least three different calendar months? Show their IDs and names.
tests.reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name FROM customers c WHERE (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT substr(o.ordered_at, 1, 7)) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id) >= 3 ORDER BY c.customer_id

tests.question: How many products have a stock quantity greater than the average stock quantity of all products?
tests.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products WHERE stock_quantity > (SELECT AVG(stock_quantity) FROM products)

tests.question: For each product category, show the total quantity sold in delivered orders.
tests.reference_sql: SELECT c.name AS category_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS quantity_sold FROM categories c JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name ORDER BY quantity_sold DESC, c.category_id

tests.question: Which suppliers have at least five products currently in stock? Show supplier IDs, names, and the number of in-stock products.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT s.supplier_id, s.name, COUNT(p.product_id) AS in_stock_products
FROM suppliers s
JOIN products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
WHERE p.stock_quantity > 0
GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.name
HAVING COUNT(p.product_id) >= 5
ORDER BY in_stock_products DESC, s.supplier_id

tests.question: How many orders are there for each order status? Show the status and order count.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count
            FROM orders
            GROUP BY status
            ORDER BY order_count DESC, status

tests.question: What was the total value of delivered order items for each month? Show the month and revenue in cents.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT substr(o.ordered_at, 1, 7) AS order_month,
                   SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price_cents) AS revenue_cents
            FROM orders o
            JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
            WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
            GROUP BY substr(o.ordered_at, 1, 7)
            ORDER BY order_month

tests.question: Find active products that have between 1 and 5 units in stock, inclusive. Show their names and stock quantities.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT name, stock_quantity
            FROM products
            WHERE is_active = 1
              AND stock_quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 5
            ORDER BY stock_quantity, name

tests.question: Which customers have written at least three product reviews and have an average rating of at least 4? Show their names, review counts, and average ratings.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id,
                   c.full_name,
                   COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count,
                   ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS average_rating
            FROM customers c
            JOIN reviews r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
            GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name
            HAVING COUNT(r.review_id) >= 3
               AND AVG(r.rating) >= 4
            ORDER BY average_rating DESC, review_count DESC, c.customer_id

tests.question: For each city, calculate the total value of delivered order items in cents. Include only cities with at least five delivered orders. Show the city, number of delivered orders, and revenue.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT c.city,
                   COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS delivered_order_count,
                   SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price_cents) AS revenue_cents
            FROM customers c
            JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
            JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
            WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
            GROUP BY c.city
            HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) >= 5
            ORDER BY revenue_cents DESC, c.city

tests.question: Which products have a price higher than the average price of products in their own category? Show product name, category, and price in cents.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT p.name AS product_name,
                   c.name AS category_name,
                   p.price_cents
            FROM products p
            JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
            WHERE p.price_cents > (
                SELECT AVG(p2.price_cents)
                FROM products p2
                WHERE p2.category_id = p.category_id
            )
            ORDER BY c.name, p.price_cents DESC, p.product_id

tests.question: How many customers are registered in each city? Show cities with at least five customers.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customer_count
            FROM customers
            GROUP BY city
            HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
            ORDER BY customer_count DESC, city

tests.question: List orders that have a payment record with a failed status. Show order ID, customer ID, order status, and payment amount in cents.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.order_id,
                   o.customer_id,
                   o.status AS order_status,
                   p.amount_cents
            FROM orders o
            JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
            WHERE p.status = 'failed'
            ORDER BY o.order_id

tests.question: How many orders were placed in each month of 2026? Show the month and order count.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT substr(ordered_at, 1, 7) AS order_month,
                   COUNT(*) AS order_count
            FROM orders
            WHERE ordered_at >= '2026-01-01'
              AND ordered_at < '2027-01-01'
            GROUP BY substr(ordered_at, 1, 7)
            ORDER BY order_month

tests.question: Which customers have placed orders but have never received a delivered shipment? Show their customer IDs and names.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name
            FROM customers c
            WHERE EXISTS (
                SELECT 1
                FROM orders o
                WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id
            )
            AND NOT EXISTS (
                SELECT 1
                FROM orders o
                JOIN shipments s ON s.order_id = o.order_id
                WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id
                  AND s.status = 'delivered'
            )
            ORDER BY c.customer_id

tests.question: For each payment status, show the number of payments and the total payment amount in cents.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT status,
                   COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
                   SUM(amount_cents) AS total_amount_cents
            FROM payments
            GROUP BY status
            ORDER BY payment_count DESC, status

tests.question: Which coupons have been used in at least three orders? Show the coupon code and number of orders using it.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT cp.code,
       COUNT(o.order_id) AS usage_count
FROM coupons cp
JOIN orders o ON o.coupon_id = cp.coupon_id
GROUP BY cp.coupon_id, cp.code
HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 3
ORDER BY usage_count DESC, cp.code

tests.question: For each product category, show the average review rating and the number of reviews. Include only categories with at least ten reviews.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT c.name AS category_name,
                   ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS average_rating,
                   COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count
            FROM categories c
            JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
            JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = p.product_id
            GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name
            HAVING COUNT(r.review_id) >= 10
            ORDER BY average_rating DESC, review_count DESC, c.name

tests.question: For each shipping carrier, show the number of shipments and the number that have been delivered.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT carrier,
                   COUNT(*) AS shipment_count,
                   SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'delivered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_count
            FROM shipments
            GROUP BY carrier
            ORDER BY shipment_count DESC, carrier

tests.question: Which products have generated more than 100000 cents in item revenue from delivered orders? Show product names and revenue in cents.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT p.product_id,
                   p.name AS product_name,
                   SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price_cents) AS revenue_cents
            FROM products p
            JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
            JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
            WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
            GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name
            HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price_cents) > 100000
            ORDER BY revenue_cents DESC, p.product_id

tests.question: For each supplier country, show the number of suppliers and the number of products they supply.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT s.country,
                   COUNT(DISTINCT s.supplier_id) AS supplier_count,
                   COUNT(p.product_id) AS product_count
            FROM suppliers s
            LEFT JOIN products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
            GROUP BY s.country
            ORDER BY product_count DESC, s.country

tests.question: Which customers have placed at least four orders? Show their IDs, names, and order counts.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id,
                   c.full_name,
                   COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count
            FROM customers c
            JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
            GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name
            HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 4
            ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.customer_id

tests.question: Which products have never received a review? Show their product IDs and names.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT p.product_id, p.name
            FROM products p
            WHERE NOT EXISTS (
                SELECT 1
                FROM reviews r
                WHERE r.product_id = p.product_id
            )
            ORDER BY p.product_id

tests.question: For each shipping carrier, calculate the average number of days between shipment and delivery, using only delivered shipments.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT carrier,
                   ROUND(AVG(julianday(delivered_at) - julianday(shipped_at)), 2) AS average_delivery_days
            FROM shipments
            WHERE status = 'delivered'
              AND shipped_at IS NOT NULL
              AND delivered_at IS NOT NULL
            GROUP BY carrier
            ORDER BY average_delivery_days, carrier

tests.question: For each product category, calculate the revenue from delivered order items. Show the category name and revenue in cents.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT c.name AS category_name,
                   SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price_cents) AS revenue_cents
            FROM categories c
            JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
            JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
            JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
            WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
            GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name
            ORDER BY revenue_cents DESC, c.category_id

tests.question: Show the ten most expensive active products, including their names, prices in cents, and stock quantities.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT name, price_cents, stock_quantity
            FROM products
            WHERE is_active = 1
            ORDER BY price_cents DESC, product_id
            LIMIT 10

tests.question: What is the average discount percentage among active coupons?
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(discount_percent), 2) AS average_discount_percent
            FROM coupons
            WHERE is_active = 1

tests.question: For each category, show the minimum and maximum product prices in cents, considering active products only.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT c.name AS category_name,
                   MIN(p.price_cents) AS minimum_price_cents,
                   MAX(p.price_cents) AS maximum_price_cents
            FROM categories c
            JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
            WHERE p.is_active = 1
            GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name
            ORDER BY c.name

tests.question: Which customers have purchased products from at least four different categories in delivered orders? Show customer IDs and names.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id,
                   c.full_name,
                   COUNT(DISTINCT p.category_id) AS category_count
            FROM customers c
            JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
            JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
            JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
            WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
            GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name
            HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category_id) >= 4
            ORDER BY category_count DESC, c.customer_id

tests.question: For each order status, show the average number of items per order, counting item quantities rather than order-item rows.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT o.status,
                   ROUND(AVG(order_totals.total_quantity), 2) AS average_items_per_order
            FROM orders o
            JOIN (
                SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS total_quantity
                FROM order_items
                GROUP BY order_id
            ) AS order_totals ON order_totals.order_id = o.order_id
            GROUP BY o.status
            ORDER BY average_items_per_order DESC, o.status
